subject: Model shortlist, context tradeoffs, and throughput estimates for FinLytics onboarding
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model shortlist, context tradeoffs, and throughput estimates for FinLytics onboarding

Hi Susan —

Following our discovery call, attached is a concise slate of model candidates plus early token-volume samples for the pipeline you described (document attached: finlytics_model_slate_v1.xlsx, token_volume_samples.csv). Key points up front:

- Use case: account aggregation + guided QA and enrichment on historical statements (mixed structured & unstructured). Expected per-session context: 1–2 documents (~3–6k tokens) plus recent conversation history (1–2k tokens).
- Candidate models we recommend for evaluation (their tradeoffs):
  1) Mosaic-Refined-Chat-13B (8k window) — best latency/cost balance for retrieval-augmented flows; good instruction-following and cheaper at scale.
  2) Llama-2-70B-Chat (32k window) — for long-document summarization / single-shot reconciliation; higher cost, better for long windows.
  3) RedInstruct-7B-QL4 (quantized) — ultra-low cost for routing/classification / short answers, limited long-context behavior.

Preliminary traffic assumptions (see token_volume_samples.csv):
- Pilot month: 50k active users, avg 3 sessions/user/month, avg tokens/session (prompt + completion) = 4k => ~600M tokens/month.
- Peak concurrency estimate: ~120 qps (peak hour), average qps 20–30.

Operational asks / decisions we need from your side to finalize sizing:
1) Confirm expected retention window for documents (do you need 30k token windows for any route?).
2) Expected % of sessions needing long summarization vs short answers (ballpark: 5% long, 80% short, 15% medium?).
3) Any hard latency SLOs (p95) for interactive sessions?

Next steps I propose:
- Quick internal evaluation: run Mosaic-Refined-Chat-13B and RedInstruct-7B-QL4 on a 1-week sample to validate token cost and latency.
- We’ll produce a recommended pilot configuration (model + quantization profile + cache policy + estimated committed capacity).

Attachments: finlytics_model_slate_v1.xlsx, token_volume_samples.csv

Thanks — happy to jump back on a short call if you prefer.

—
David Kim
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@finlytics.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@finlytics.com>, procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 12:38:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist, context tradeoffs, and throughput estimates for FinLytics onboarding

Thanks David — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick clarifications:

1) Document retention: we plan to keep 18 months of customer statements; for the MVP we can scope to 12 months but must support a full-run summary that may require up to ~18k tokens in some cases.
2) Session mix: current product analytics suggest ~10% long summaries, ~65% multi-turn QA (short/medium), ~25% quick classification/routing.
3) Latency SLOs: product wants interactive p95 <= 450ms for short returns, <= 1.2s for medium, long summaries can be batched async (acceptable up to 6s).

Procurement asked for: a mutual action plan (timeline / milestones), an initial SOW to review, and clarity on what logs/audit artifacts we will receive for SOC/infosec review. If you can prod Marissa on the MS/ops plan I’ll loop procurement on the SOW review.

Also: are you recommending a hybrid approach (dedicated for long summarization + hosted for chat) to balance cost?

—
Susan Lee
Head of Product, FinLytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@finlytics.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist, context tradeoffs, and throughput estimates for FinLytics onboarding

Hi Susan — thanks for the fast answers, that helps a lot. Operational recommendations from the CS/implementation side given the mix and SLOs you described: 

Summary of recommendation:
- Pilot (MVP): Mosaic-Refined-Chat-13B (8k window) for interactive and multi-turn QA; RedInstruct-7B-QL4 for routing/classification paths. Use Llama-2-70B-Chat as a background worker for on-demand long-document single-shot summarization jobs (async queue).

Sizing rationale & throughput controls:
- Interactive route (65% of traffic): assume avg 2.5k tokens/session; target p95 <= 450ms requires continuous batching + prefix KV cache enabled. Expect ~40–60 tokens/ms cost on our runtime for the 13B profile; we estimate ~80 inference vCPUs / 4 dedicated GPU acceleration slots during peak hour to hold p95 under 450ms with caching enabled.
- Long summary jobs (10%): run on a separate dedicated pool (1–2 large-context nodes) in async mode to avoid impacting interactive latency. Use sequence-slicing and progressive summarization to keep memory footprint manageable for the 32k windows.

Pilot run plan (2–4 weeks):
1) Week 0: share small data sample (anonymized) and confirm 1k session traces — David will coordinate test payloads.
2) Week 1: smoke test both candidate models with 1k synthetic sessions; return latency & cost CSVs.
3) Week 2: run 3-day peak simulation (ramp to 120 qps) to validate autoscaling and cache hit ratios.
4) Deliverable: pilot report + recommended committed capacity (including suggested Dedicated pods for steady-state).

Compliance / logs: we’ll produce audit logs (request ids, model versions, timestamps) and a short SOC/infosec checklist. I attached a draft SLA we typically use so procurement has something to react to (attachment: sla-draft-finlytics.pdf).

Questions for you (FinLytics):
- Can procurement sign off on a 3-month pilot with a capped pilot spend?
- Any hard restrictions on bringing data into a dedicated environment (VPC)? If yes we’ll plan Private deployment options.

Happy to host a technical handoff call with your infra team this week to walk through KV caching and batching knobs.

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist, context tradeoffs, and throughput estimates for FinLytics onboarding

Thanks all — quick commercial follow-up as we lock the technical approach.

- Pricing & capacity: given the pilot scope (~600M tokens/month projected), two commercial paths look reasonable:
  A) Hosted + burst: no commit, pay-as-you-go for the Mosaic-Refined-Chat-13B + RedInstruct-7B routes. Good for flexibility; expect higher per-token unit price during sustained peak.
  B) Dedicated reserve (recommended for predictable unit economics): commit to a 6-month reserved pool sized for 60–70% of expected steady-state peak (we’ll size pods after pilot simulation). This reduces per-token compute unit costs by ~18–25% depending on commitment level.

- SOW / Procurement items:
  * We’ll provide an SOW draft and an explicit runbook for onboarding (links above).
  * Procurement needs the SLA + sample audit logs and the draft pricing terms; Marissa attached the SLA PDF.
  * If FinLytics prefers a hybrid deployment (private for long-doc summarization + hosted for interactive chat), we’ll include the Private deployment add-on pricing in the SOW.

Next steps I will take: prepare a short mutual action plan doc and a draft SOW (DocuSign link included) for your legal/procurement to review. Marissa — can you confirm the pilot spend cap figure for the SOW?

Regards,
Ben Carter
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
